quotes.text: No, we need to modernize every single policy we have to reflect a world in which AI exists, and just getting [Congress] to understand that basic principle is the most frustrating part of my job.

As I mentioned earlier, like any tool, AI can bring extraordinary benefits. But, like any tool, it can also be weaponized. It can also bring challenges that we can't anticipate. And so I think it's really important that Congress plays a role in helping to figure out those guardrails around questions like, "how do we ensure whether an algorithm has a diversity of data so that it's not sort of unwittingly, for lack of a better word, inserting bias into something?"

And given the increased use of AI in applications that include healthcare, criminal justice, decisionmaking, there is a huge potential for algorithmic bias to exacerbate social inequities. Can you talk about NIST's work to develop guidance to help organizations that make algorithms avoid this garbage in, garbage out problem?

At the launch of NIST's AI Risk Management Framework, Dr. Alondra Nelson, the former acting Director of OSTP, noted that AI tools are too often developed without the input or the consent of the people whose lives they will touch. Can you discuss how NIST's budget supports broad public engagement to ensure that diverse perspectives are incorporated in these frameworks?

Today, @HouseScience spoke with @NIST Director Dr. Laurie Locascio on NIST's FY 24 budget proposal. 

I asked Dr. Locascio about NIST’s efforts to manage algorithmic bias in AI systems & how their organization plans to expand advancement opportunities for women employees. https://t.co/VsOWuTilUy

I introduced a bill with @RepNateMoran, @SenBrianSchatz and @SteveDaines to protect Americans from unsolicited lewd photos.

Our bill will BAN cyberflashing and the transfer of unsolicited AI-generated explicit photos that have been proliferating throughout social media recently. https://t.co/9BchWPKQG8

Too many Americans have experienced cyberflashing & other forms of online sexual harassment. My bipartisan, bicameral CONSENT Act will ban cyberflashing & the transfer of unsolicited AI-generated explicit photos. 
I’m grateful to @Bumble for their support. https://t.co/Azf4ZDUylV

With the widespread adoption of social media and dating apps and the rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence and machine learning, cyberflashing and other forms of online sexual exploitation are rising.

And, General Kruse, how is the Defense Intelligence Enterprise looking to incorporate emerging technology such as AI into its capabilities, and to ensure that these new capabilities will provide the most relevant information for our warfighters? General Kruse. Thank you for the question. We have established an emerging and disruptive technologies organization that is focused really in three areas: one is on quantum, and that is doing some really good work on how others are using quantum computing, quantum comms, and quantum sensing. We have an organization that is focused on biotechnology and biosecurity. And then another group that is working specifically on AI and counter-AI. And we can certainly talk through what some of those lines of efforts might look like.
what steps are you taking to ensure that you can identify misinformation that our adversaries may be using through AI?

Today, the House Armed Services Subcommittee on Intelligence and Special Operations received testimony on @DefenseIntel's efforts to combat incoming threats.

Listen to my questions on how the Intelligence Community is collaborating amidst those threats and emerging tech like AI: https://t.co/XsBNJ6CGpZ

The Science Committee advanced a slate of bills to advance American research on AI, nuclear energy, and natural disasters.

One bill included as an amendment my BUILT Act, which addresses infrastructure risks caused by climate change. https://t.co/9ZVbM5POKe

And Dr. Schmidt, I am glad you stayed, because in your opening statement you said that the sheer speed of AI development is outpacing our societal and government ability to adapt, and I wholeheartedly agree with you. [...] And I came to the conclusion 7 years ago that none of our systems in the United States at all—government, education, none of them—are prepared for what is coming.

AI has the ability to transform everything, and we are in a race for global AI dominance against China. Yet the Trump Administration has undermined our ability to compete through its tariffs, war on renewable energy, mass firings and funding freezes.

Losing the AI competition to China threatens our economy and national security. I joined @EnergyCommerce to address this critical issue.

And how should the United States be preparing itself for both the potential of AI-enhanced cyber attacks on critical infrastructure and the possibility of more coordinated cyber attacks amongst multiple hostile foreign adversaries?

I want to start with Ms. Galante. Can you expand on what you mentioned in your testimony regarding the availability of AI to improve data processing capabilities to allow even unsophisticated adversaries to more effectively extract key insights from stolen data and how worried we should be that AI will also greatly expand the ability of adversaries to get around our cyber defenses and commit even more devastating cyber attacks?

This year’s theme for #WorldPressFreedomDay focuses on the challenges of preserving freedoms of the press and expression in the midst of the explosive growth of AI. Like any tool, AI can bring great innovation and progress, but great harm if we are not careful. 

As an @EnergyCommerce member, I am focused on ensuring that we can harness the power of AI as a tool to enhance, not erode, our fundamental first amendment freedoms.

Learn more about the impact of AI on freedom of the press and media ⬇️

AI is revolutionizing everything, and the U.S. must meet the energy demand needed to meet this moment without increasing prices and health risks for American families or further endangering our planet.

Read my op-ed in @WashTimes about how clean and renewable energy will prepare us for the AI age.

AI is revolutionizing all aspects of our lives. Like any tool, it can cause great harm if used without any guardrails. After years of Congressional inaction, states have stepped up to regulate AI to protect our privacy, public safety and more. House Republicans voted to stop them for 10 years. I joined @EnergyCommerce Democrats to fight back.

And we talked about—then, we were in the fourth Industrial Revolution, and we talked about how with each Industrial Revolution, just as it brought extraordinary advancements, they brought extraordinary challenges. I don't know if we are on the way to the fifth Industrial Revolution with the transition from 5G to 6G and how fast AI is evolving, but I think we are woefully behind getting ahead of the challenges. [...] where Dario Amodei said that AI could wipe out half of all entry-level white-collar jobs and spike unemployment to 10 to 20 percent in the next 1 to 5 years.

AI has the power to transform every aspect of our lives for the better, but also will bring extraordinary challenges from job losses, explosive energy demand, new cybersecurity challenges, and more.

At today’s Energy & Commerce subcommittee hearing on AI, I focused my questions on how policy makers and industry can get ahead of these challenges.

Congratulations, Akash Arun Kumar Soumya for winning the Congressional App Challenge for Virginia’s Fourth!

Akash designed ElderLink AR, an app that uses AI to deliver wellness guidance for seniors and real-time exercise feedback. His project bridges mental and physical health for aging adults — way to go!

Increased data usage through increased use of the internet and AI requires more data centers, exploding demand on our eclectic grid. We must not only generate more energy, but also manage demand to meet our needs affordably. Yet the Department of Energy cancelled grants and projects intended to do just that. No wonder energy prices rose as much as 13% in 2025.

Today, I joined @EnergyCommerce Democrats to push back on these and other Trump Administration actions that undermine efforts to meet energy demand affordably.

As AI rapidly changes our telecommunications networks, Congress must understand how these networks adapt, the risks that may emerge and what responsible use should look like. 

Today, I introduced the bipartisan AI-Ready Networks Act with @JayObernolte to examine AI use in telecommunication networks and the implications for security, reliability and the workforce.

AI’s impacts on our workforce and technological landscape cannot be overstated, and we must act now to ensure these changes both strengthen our telecommunications ecosystem and benefit the American people. This bipartisan bill will ensure Congress has the information it needs to assess best practices for the use of AI, support innovation in telecommunications networks and improve transparency for the public.

As a prosecutor, advocate for abused children and state senator representing Loudoun County, Jennifer Wexton built a career around protecting others before representing Virginia’s Tenth Congressional District from 2019 to 2025. After being diagnosed with progressive supranuclear palsy, she continued serving with resilience and became the first member of Congress to speak on the House floor using an AI-generated voice.

With energy demand on the rise and new emerging technologies like AI and data centers changing the energy landscape, Congress needs to partner with state and local governments to address rising costs and ensure a cleaner energy future.

This morning, I joined @axios’ @sabrinaamorenoo for an #AxiosLive conversation about the impact on Virginia, the data center capital of the world, and beyond.
Yes we are in a race with China on AI, but if we win the race in a way that exhausts our natural resources, that makes our grid less reliable, then will we have really won that race?

This year, I secured over $10 million in Community Project Funding to benefit communities across Virginia’s Fourth.

This week, I presented over $1 million to @Hopewell_VA for stormwater infrastructure improvements and over $1 million to @VSU_1882 to launch its Center for Generative AI and Industrial Cybersecurity.

This center is going to ensure that all of the policy and legal and ethical framework that has governed human interactions also governs AI … that we are able to ensure that human beings control AI and not the other way around.

As the American people struggle to pay their energy bills, they should not have to bear the burden of meeting the energy needs of data centers and AI.

Yesterday, the Energy Subcommittee advanced several bills to help ensure they don’t. https://t.co/bfvFBw6ppb

OpenAI and Anthropic recently reported disturbing incidents where advanced AI models broke out of isolated test environments to access the internet and hack third-party networks without authorization. 

Last week, I joined @RepCasar and several @HouseDemocrats colleagues in letters to OpenAI’s CEO demanding answers and calling on Speaker Johnson to convene hearings with the large AI companies’ CEOs to understand how these incidents occurred and ways to prevent cybersecurity threats posed by AI. 

I joined @Bloomberg’s Balance of Power to discuss the letters and why we need Congressional hearings now.

Jason Coxon’s warning that AI could kill us all by the end of the decade has made clear that that power that President Kennedy discussed has now been given to AI. And just like the nuclear arms race and the space race with Russia required guardrails to balance the benefits and the harms of nuclear technology and space exploration, so does the AI race with China.

We have one chance to get this right, and we must be deliberate and take control for any unintended consequences for risk. Rogue AI upending every sector from health care and national security to transportation and banking and more. I can’t support Representative Evans’ bill expanding open AI without any guardrails to responsibly address not only its benefits, but the threats, because those threats are existential, those threats are as real as the threats around nuclear power gone rogue.

And this is why the federal government, especially Congress, has a responsibility to lead by example and heeding these calls to step up, not abdicate our oversight and regulatory authority to another branch of government, particularly when the president thinks this is all a hoax and a conspiracy.

This is deeply alarming. 

It’s past time we demand greater government oversight of AI before the quest for profit ends humanity. https://t.co/UAzsvW2ItR

Like any tool, AI has the potential for transformative benefits and harms. Last week, a former Anthropic employee went public with concerns that AI could “kill us all by the end of the decade.”  Since then, similar concerns raised by AI leaders and calls for greater government oversight have been dismissed as a "conspiracy." 

AI experts warned of the need to ensure humans, not machines, remain in control in the AI industry 17 months ago during an Energy & Commerce hearing. 

Today, @energycommerce Dems called for comprehensive action now.

In a rapidly growing digital world in which U.S. households have on average 21 devices connected to the Internet, more and more activities from health care delivery to banking are conducted online and AI and other advanced technology continue to advance, the number of data centers has grown at a more rapid pace than our current electric infrastructure can handle.

Like any tool, AI has the potential for good and harm. Experts have repeatedly warned that we need federal action to prevent the harms.

ICYMI: I joined @alivitali on @WayTooEarly to call in Congress to act. https://t.co/UI3NGq9uRE

The CEOs of Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI have called for greater government oversight of frontier AI models. President Trump dismissed these concerns as a “conspiracy.” Congress seems asleep at the wheel.

Read more in my newsletter below ⬇️
Congress should examine every public policy and issue area to address how AI can be used as a tool for both good and harm.

Advancements in AI and robotics contain great potential for the future of our increasingly digital world, but also pose great risks if left unchecked and unregulated.

I joined @jameshohmann at @PostLive’s AI Edge Summit for a 1-on-1 discussion on why Congress must act to harness the best in these new technologies and place guardrails to avoid potential harms.
